title: Bur Oak: Ancient Prairie Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: The prairie oak, with bark built to survive grass fires. The Big Tree near Columbia, Missouri, was about 200 years old when Lewis and Clark passed.
intro: The bur oak is the prairie oak, its bark thick enough to survive the grass fires that once kept the American Midwest open, so the old ones are survivors of the savanna that cities were built across. The Big Tree in the Missouri river bottoms near McBaine was already about two hundred years old when Lewis and Clark came up the river in 1804; it is 7.3 metres round and the national champion of its species. In Indianapolis, Mae Kile refused to sell her house to anyone who would not promise to keep the oak. Chicago keeps several. One in the grove on Wooded Island blew down around 2016 and its rings were counted back to roughly 1730, and the oak on the Midway Plaisance was the one tree left standing when the ground was cleared for the 1893 World's Fair.
